text:
maria: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — long-running generation (customer says ~80-120s) times out mid-stream and they see multiple tokens billed. They opened a billing dispute. Attached logs below.
sam: can you paste the SDK version + the timeout config they're using? also whether they're using sync vs async and streaming vs non-streaming.
maria: customer is on python sdk 0.3.1 (installed via pip). sync client, streaming true. they set a dict timeout like this:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout={"connect": 2, "read": 30, "write": 60})
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-v1", prompt=prompt, stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    handle(chunk)
```
They said the stream raises after ~30s with a ReadTimeoutError and then the SDK appears to retry the request, which results in a second charge and a new generation starting.
maria: logs (redacted):
```
ERROR:root:Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    for chunk in resp:
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/streaming.py", line 120, in __iter__
    chunk = self._iter_next()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/_exceptions.py", line 37, in __raise_for_status
httpx.ReadTimeout: Stream read exceeded 30.0s
INFO:root:Retrying generate (attempt 1) -> new request id req_ABC123
```
sam: two things to check here: 1) python sdks historically treat the top-level `timeout` similarly to httpx (connect/read/write). For streaming, the `read` timeout applies per-chunk. If your model produces long gaps, increase `read` or set it to `None` for streaming. 2) there's a known issue in 0.3.1 where the client-level retry logic can start a retry after a streaming read timeout — effectively re-sending the request which explains the duplicate charge. Workarounds: set `retries=0` on the client or include an `idempotency_key` in the generate call.
liam: confirming: bug filed as RED-IO-482. Fix landed on main and is included in the 0.4.x release line. We plan a 0.3.x backport patch (0.3.3) but timeline is 48-72 hours. For immediate mitigation recommend upgrade to 0.4.1+ or use the following temporary config:
```
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout={"connect":2, "read":120, "write":120}, retries=0)
# or
resp = client.generate(..., stream=True, idempotency_key="acmecorp-incident-2026-03-17")
```
nisha: billing note — if their invoice shows duplicate charges and they provide the two request ids (req_ABC123 and req_DEF456) we can credit the duplicate. Please collect request ids and timestamps; we'll need the customer consent for a refund. I can open a billing case once we have that.
maria: customer provided the two ids and timestamps. I asked them to try upgrading to 0.4.1 first and to try the retries=0 workaround if they can't upgrade. I also shared the idempotency header approach.
support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-2026-1432 assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml. Labels: bug, billing, high-priority.
sam: for repro (engineering): minimal repro to reproduce fast — use a prompt that yields long silence and a small chunk size so the read gap > read timeout. Example:
```
# repro.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout={"connect":2, "read":5, "write":60}, retries=1)
prompt = "<generate a long monologue with pauses>\n" * 1
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-test-lag", prompt=prompt, stream=True)
for i, chunk in enumerate(resp):
    print(i, chunk.text)
    if i>20: break
```
This reproduces the stream read timeout quickly in our env. Engineers: note that lowering `read` helps surface the issue quicker.
liam: I'll prioritize the 0.3.x backport. Also adding a server-side guard to ensure duplicate billing isn't recorded when identical idempotency keys are present.
maria: customer upgraded to 0.4.1 and reported they no longer saw mid-stream aborts within their normal workload. They accepted a credit for the duplicate charge. nisha — billing case reference BL-6678.
maria: thanks all — closing the escalation after backport/public patch and customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
